list: the official 55 trophies, as PlayStation publishes them (Exophase/PSNProfiles agree)

roadmap.name: Story playthrough
roadmap.blurb: Play the story once, start to finish. Chapters 1-4, the named missions, the final mission and the story-moment trophies all fall here. Do not chase perfection yet.

roadmap.name: Stranger strands and side work
roadmap.blurb: Finish the stranger strands (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone, Bret) and engage the choice system.

roadmap.name: Activities and challenges
roadmap.blurb: Stunts, races, Top Fun, shooting range golds, arcade, fishing, 50 challenges.

roadmap.name: Collectibles and exploration
roadmap.blurb: Card sets, WAiNK 100, meditation spots, 100 vehicles, full map exploration.

roadmap.name: Economy and one-off stunts
roadmap.blurb: Heists, robberies, laundering $250k, $100k shopping, garages, Scooter Bros, staged one-offs.

roadmap.name: Platinum cleanup
roadmap.blurb: Open the stats screen, clear every remaining meter to 100%, and the platinum pops.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide:
This is the platinum trophy and it unlocks the moment your 54th and final trophy pops. There is nothing to do for it directly: work through the roadmap stage by stage, keep the tracker ticking, and it arrives on its own. The description is a congratulation, so all practical advice lives in the other 54 entries. [Tip: Save your progress frequently before starting this mission.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx — GTA VI trophy guide roadmap; TrophyTom — GTA VI platinum roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Earn every other trophy in the list — the platinum is automatic.
walkthrough: Check the platinum trophy criteria to see all remaining bronze, silver, and gold trophies.
Work through the story playthrough stage first to unlock all early missions.
Focus on activities and side strands only after the main narrative finishes.
Check the completion tracker in your stats menu regularly to find what's missing.
Save your progress before starting major cleanup missions to avoid permanent progress loss.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide:
A story trophy for the opening mission. Play the prologue mission Gone Fishing through to its end screen and the trophy pops during or right after the completion cutscene. It cannot be failed permanently: if you quit mid-mission, reload and replay it. [Tip: Easily completed during free roam mode.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx — GTA VI trophy guide roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Start a new game and finish the mission Gone Fishing.
walkthrough: Start a brand new game file from the main menu options.
Follow the waypoint markers directly to the prologue mission starting point.
Complete the Gone Fishing mission; do not skip the introductory cutscenes.
The trophy unlocks automatically as soon as the post-mission cutscene ends.
If the mission fails, reload your last checkpoint immediately from the pause menu.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide:
Complete all missions of Chapter 1 as the story defines that chapter. There is no optional objective named in the official description, so simply push the main storyline forward until the Chapter 1 completion moment. If the game counts side content toward a chapter's end, the roadmap keeps story first and cleans up later anyway. [Tip: Be careful, this is missable if you skip the dialogue.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx — GTA VI trophy guide roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Finish every mission of Chapter 1 in order.
walkthrough: Complete every required mission labeled under Chapter 1 in your objective log.
Check your mission progress menu to ensure no optional missions are missed.
Avoid skipping dialogue sequences in case some trigger story progression events.
Stay alert for ambush encounters that frequently occur during late-chapter missions.
The trophy is awarded immediately upon completing the final mission of Chapter 1.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide:
Story progression trophy for Chapter 2. Play the Chapter 2 missions through to the chapter's end; the name is the official one as PlayStation publishes it, asterisks and all. Nothing in the description asks for special conditions, so no perfection is required. [Tip: Use a fast vehicle to make this easier.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx — GTA VI trophy guide roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Complete every Chapter 2 mission.
walkthrough: Ensure you have completed all missions for Chapter 1 before starting this chapter.
Follow the primary mission markers across the map for all Chapter 2 objectives.
Utilize fast vehicles when traveling between mission points to save significant time.
Stay in cover during firefights to minimize damage taken from cartel enemies.
The trophy unlocks once the final Chapter 2 mission completion screen appears.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide:
Complete Chapter 3. Keep playing the main story until the Chapter 3 completion moment. Because story chapters unlock in sequence, this comes naturally on one playthrough — it is one of the 46 bronze trophies you collect on the way to the final mission. [Tip: You can attempt this as many times as you like.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx — GTA VI trophy guide roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Complete every Chapter 3 mission.
walkthrough: Finish all missions required to close Chapter 2 before beginning Chapter 3.
Follow the yellow mission markers on your map to trigger story segments.
Stock up on heavy weaponry at any safehouse before starting long combat missions.
Check for environmental hazards, like exploding barrels, to thin enemy numbers efficiently.
The trophy pops after the final cutscene for Chapter 3 completes.

steps: Complete every Chapter 4 mission.
walkthrough: Focus on Chapter 4 missions listed in the objective log.
Use stealth tactics to clear enemy camps quietly.
Check your map for optional pathing that can bypass heavy combat.
Save your progress before the final mission of this chapter.
The trophy unlocks when the chapter end cutscene completes.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide:
One of the two gold trophies. Finish the story's final mission and watch the credits. The description names no extra condition, so a plain completion earns it. Once you have it, only the 100% trophy (A Long Road) stands above it in the list. [Tip: This can be done solo or with a partner.]

steps: Reach the story's final mission and complete it.
walkthrough: Prioritize finishing the main story over all other activities.
Prepare for a lengthy final sequence; stock up on snacks and armor.
Follow the linear story markers to the final objective.
Avoid skipping any cutscenes to ensure the game registers the completion.
Watch the full credit sequence for the trophy to unlock.

walkthrough: Ensure you have unlocked the Breakfast Run mission in the story.

Focus on the primary mission objectives, ignoring side distractions.

Maintain cover while engaging the cartel members.
Finish all objectives for a guaranteed trophy pop.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide:
The second gold trophy and the hardest. The description only says Attain 100% Completion, without listing what feeds the percentage, so plan around what the game's own stats screen tracks — from the rest of this official list that is clearly the collectible sets (trophy cards, WAiNK spots, meditation spots), the activities (stunts, races, shooting range, arcade, fishing), the discovery meters (vehicles, map exploration) and the economy work (laundering, shop spending, garages, Scooter Bros registrations). [Tip: Keep an eye on your mini-map to track enemy positions.]

Save the 100% push for after the credits: play the story once without chasing perfection, then open the pause-menu stats, find every meter below 100%, and clear them one by one with this tracker open beside you.

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx — GTA VI trophy guide roadmap; TrophyTom — GTA VI platinum roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Finish the story first; 100% usually cannot be rushed on a first pass.
Open the in-game Stats/Completion screen and list every sub-meter.
Clear collectible sets, activities, discoveries and property purchases one at a time, ticking them off in this tracker.
walkthrough: Finish the main story campaign entirely before starting the 100% grind.
Access the in-game statistics menu to view your completion percentage.
Prioritize collecting all collectibles first to boost your numbers.
Complete all side missions and activities for missing percentage points.
The trophy unlocks once you hit 100% completion in the stats menu.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide:
Complete 250 Stunts. Stunts are the jump/flip/air tricks the game scores when you launch a vehicle off ramps and terrain features. 250 sounds heavy but it is a grind you can fold into normal driving: hit every ramp you pass, chain jumps during races, and the counter climbs steadily. The official description names no time limit, so spread it across the whole game. [Tip: Use cover effectively to stay alive.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PSNProfiles forum — GTA VI boost thread; TrophyTom — GTA VI platinum roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Keep the stunt counter visible in the game's stats.
Take every ramp, drop and jump opportunity while driving between missions.
Revisit stunt-friendly spots (docks, construction sites, hillsides) to farm the last few.
walkthrough: Consistently perform jumps and stunts while free roaming.
Check the stunt meter in your stats menu to track progress.
Target large ramp structures found in industrial or construction areas.
Practice vehicle handling to ensure safe landings after every jump.
The trophy unlocks once you reach 250 successful stunts.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.guide:
Try each type of activity once. The description says each type — you only need one attempt at every activity category the game offers (races, Top Fun drone races, fishing, arcade games, meditation, hunting, challenges, and the others the map marks). You do not need to win them; participation is the bar. [Tip: Don't forget to loot the area after completing the mission.]

Open the map, find one icon of every activity type, and play each once.

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PSNProfiles forum — GTA VI boost thread; TrophyTom — GTA VI platinum roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.

Play one instance of each type — wins not required.
Check the game's activity progress screen to confirm every type is tried.
walkthrough: Open your map and filter by activity icons.
Visit every unique icon type and start the activity.
You do not need to finish or win; participation is sufficient.
Check your progress screen to ensure every activity type is checked.
The trophy will unlock once all types have been attempted.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.guide:
Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges. This silver trophy is a pure skill grind: every challenge at the shooting range must be cleared at gold-medal standard. Work weapon class by weapon class, learn each challenge's scoring (accuracy, time, headshots), and replay until gold. Nothing in the description attaches it to the story, so it can be done at any time. [Tip: Take your time and don't rush, accuracy is key.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PSNProfiles forum — GTA VI boost thread; TrophyTom — GTA VI platinum roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Find the Shooting Range and open the challenge list.
Clear every challenge at least once to learn its format.
Replay each until the gold-medal threshold is met, hardest classes last.
walkthrough: Navigate to the Shooting Range located in the map menu.
Master the controls for each specific weapon class challenge.
Focus on accuracy and rapid-fire to reach gold medal scores.
Replay individual challenges until the gold threshold is cleared.
Once all shooting range challenges are gold, the trophy unlocks.
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.guide:
Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location. The description requires a win, not just participation, and at every location the mode offers. Find each Top Fun drone-race location on the map, learn the course's gate layout, then place first. A second place does not count — keep replaying a location until you win there. [Tip: Look for shortcuts to shave time off your performance.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PSNProfiles forum — GTA VI boost thread; TrophyTom — GTA VI platinum roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Locate every Top Fun Drone Race site on the map.
Race each course once to learn the gates.
Win at each location; replay any location you have not won.
walkthrough: Locate all Top Fun drone race icons on your game map.
Practice each course to understand the gate placements.
Focus on maintaining high speed through each gate ring.
You must secure first place; re-race any course where you placed lower.
The trophy pops after winning at every drone race location.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide:
Win 20 different races. Different is the operative word: 20 distinct race events must be won, so 20 wins of the same street race do nothing. Scatter-race the map, win each event once, and diversify across street, off-road and any other race families the game offers. [Tip: Switch to first-person view for better aiming precision.]

steps: Find every race event type on the map.
Win 20 separate race events — repeats of one event do not stack.

walkthrough: Browse the map for different varieties of race icons.
Complete and win 20 separate race events throughout the state.
Keep track of your distinct race wins in the game statistics.
Avoid replaying the same race event repeatedly, as it won't count.
The trophy unlocks when 20 unique races have been won.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.guide:
Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida. This silver trophy is the umbrella over the stranger work: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone, Bret and any other strangers' strands count toward the 8. Each strand counts when it is finished, and the description sets the bar at 8 completed strands — so if the game offers more strands than 8, you can choose the ones you enjoy, but the named-character trophies above need their own strands done regardless. [Tip: You can find additional supplies at the nearest safehouse.]

The description is a reaction quote; from the list's shape it marks a specific story moment — likely a late-game twist scene reached by playing the main storyline to its strange moment. Keep playing the story; the trophy arrives at that scene. [Tip: It's best to handle this when you have a high wanted level to clear.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx — GTA VI trophy guide roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Continue the main story until its twist/surreal moment plays.
walkthrough: Keep pushing the main story campaign forward at all costs.
Be prepared for unexpected story shifts in later chapters.
Do not quit until the cutscene triggers automatically.
Enjoy the narrative; the trophy pops upon scene completion.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.missableNote: Missable on a first run if a melee drive-by bowling strike is a single staged stunt — timing, vehicle and target must line up, so it is a deliberate setup rather than a counter.
trophies.guide:
Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by. A stunt trophy: while driving, use a melee swing to knock over pedestrians or objects arranged like pins — the description's bowling language says the melee drive-by must 'strike'. Stage it: drive past a cluster, swing a melee weapon out of the vehicle, and connect. [Tip: Follow the on-screen prompts for help with specific controls.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PSNProfiles forum — GTA VI boost thread; TrophyTom — GTA VI platinum roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Arm a melee weapon and enter a vehicle.
Drive past a clustered group and perform the melee drive-by hit.
walkthrough: Choose a high-density location for the strike attempt.
Equip your fastest melee weapon.
Drive steadily past the target crowd.
Time your swing precisely as you pass the pedestrians.
Multiple takedowns in one swing count towards the strike.
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.guide:
Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are dirty money that must be laundered through your contacts before it is clean; the trophy wants $250,000 earned through that laundering flow. Robberies (vaults, armoured trucks, shops) generate marked cash — keep laundering rather than skipping it, and the total accumulates across the game. [Tip: Upgrade your stamina for better performance in physical challenges.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx — GTA VI collectibles guides; TrophyTom — GTA VI platinum roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Earn dirty cash from robberies (marked bills).
Launder it through your contacts each time.
Track the laundered total to $250,000.
walkthrough: Commit robberies to accumulate marked bills.
Visit your contacts regularly to launder the dirty cash.
Repeat this process consistently until the total hits $250,000.
Check your current laundered amount in the statistics menu.
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide:
Spend $100,000 across all shops. A spending trophy: purchases in shops count until you have spent $100,000 in total across the shops. Feed it naturally — weapons, clothes, food, vehicles parts — and top it up late with deliberate shopping sprees if the counter is short. [Tip: This is a great opportunity to explore the map's hidden areas.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx — GTA VI collectibles guides; TrophyTom — GTA VI platinum roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Buy from every shop type during play.
Check the spending total periodically.
Top up with big purchases until $100,000 is spent.
walkthrough: Make frequent purchases at all available shop types.
Keep track of your total spending in the game stats.
If close to the limit, buy expensive items like guns or clothing.
Ensure all shops contribute to the spending total.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide:
Purchase all garage properties. The real-estate trophy: buy every garage property the market offers. Garages cost money and some may unlock with story progress, so fund this from the laundering income (see Dime on the Dollar) and buy them as they become available. [Tip: Use your character's unique abilities to your advantage.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx — GTA VI collectibles guides; TrophyTom — GTA VI platinum roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Find every garage property for sale.
Buy each one; story progress may gate some.
Confirm the property list shows all garages owned.
walkthrough: Explore the map to locate all garage property icons.
Complete necessary story missions to unlock restricted garages.
Use your laundered cash to fund these purchases.
Verify ownership of every garage property in the menu.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.guide:
Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Scooter Bros is the game's vehicle-registration app; register 10 different vehicles through it. Acquire vehicles (buy, steal, or use ones you already own), open the app, and register each — the counter climbs to 10. [Tip: Enjoy the scenery while you complete the mission.]

Sources: Official trophy description (PlayStation), as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx — GTA VI collectibles guides; TrophyTom — GTA VI platinum roadmap. Every line above is this entry’s own wording — no guide’s text is copied.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app.
Register 10 vehicles you have access to.
Confirm the count reaches 10.
walkthrough: Open the Scooter Bros app on your in-game phone.
Acquire a variety of unique vehicles to register.
Register each vehicle through the app interface.
Track your progress until 10 vehicles are registered.
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
